page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes 614 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of strong and average performance characteristics. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, ranking in the top 25%, while multi-core CPU performance falls into the average tier. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while the PassMark memory score is strong, cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1033.28 GB/sec, and uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 38.7 GB/sec and 22.85 GB/sec respectively. Other metrics, including Geekbench compiling, Redis SET operations at 15.84 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 17.7 GB/sec, consistently align with average tier performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16ads_v5 offers high memory density and local storage capacity relative to its 16-vCPU compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous high-throughput uncached memory access. The combination of 128 GB RAM, a 614 GB local disk, and average database operation benchmarks indicates suitability for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, data processing, and general-purpose memory-intensive enterprise applications.

Operating at 3.525 GHz, it features 614 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU and PassMark memory performance, alongside average multi-core CPU, Redis, and database operation metrics.
